Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates a persistent, ill-defined opacity in the right upper lobe without significant volume loss (ruling out atelectasis) or cavitation (ruling out TB). In an adult with asthma-like symptoms and a persistent focal opacity, adenocarcinoma (specifically mucinous adenocarcinoma which can mimic pneumonia or present with aerogenous spread) is a critical diagnosis to consider, as it often presents as a non-resolving consolidation.
